dryer.note: Frigidaire publishes a dryer article titled "How To Use Your Dryer: Alarms & Codes", but its solution section is empty -- the page lists no codes. Frigidaire does publish a range code guide, so this is a gap in their laundry documentation rather than in the search.

codes.meaning: The top-load washer is taking an unusually long time to fill, pointing to a weak or interrupted water supply.
Water is draining out of the tub far slower than it should, suggesting a drain-path restriction.
The washer senses its lid is open or the lid-locking mechanism never properly engaged.
The load has shifted unevenly inside the drum during spin, throwing the machine off balance.

E4.what_it_means: The load has shifted unevenly inside the drum during spin, throwing the machine off balance.
E4.why_it_happens: Usually one heavy item on its own, or a load that has bunched to one side.
E4.what_to_try: Open the lid, redistribute the load by hand and restart the spin. Adding a similar-weight item often settles it.
E4.when_to_call: If balanced loads also trip it, the suspension is worth checking.

codes.meaning: The washer itself isn't sitting level on the floor.
The lid was left open for more than about 20 seconds while control-lock was turned on.
Too many suds in the drum, or suds overflowing, usually from non-HE detergent.
The dishwasher's door-locking feature is currently engaged.

LOC.what_it_means: Not a fault — the door-locking feature is engaged, so the controls will not respond.
LOC.why_it_happens: Normally switched on to stop a running cycle being changed, then forgotten about.
LOC.what_to_try: Hold the lock pad for a few seconds to release it; the panel returns to normal once it takes.
LOC.when_to_call: Only if the lock will not release.

codes.meaning: The dishwasher cannot confirm the door has been fully shut and latched.
The unit is pausing to heat incoming water or actively running its internal heating element.
A cycle finished without the tub fully emptying its water, pointing to a drainage problem.

i20.what_it_means: A cycle finished without the tub fully emptying, pointing to a drainage problem.
i20.why_it_happens: Usually a clogged filter, a kinked drain hose, or a disposer holding debris where the dishwasher line joins it.
i20.what_to_try: Clear the tub filter, check the drain hose for kinks, and run the disposer if the line joins one.
i20.when_to_call: If the filter and hose are clear and it still will not drain, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: Food debris has built up enough in the filter or sump area to block normal water flow.
The dishwasher lost electrical power partway through a cycle.

PF.what_it_means: Not a fault. The dishwasher lost electrical power partway through a cycle.
PF.why_it_happens: An outage, a tripped breaker, or the door opened long enough to cut the cycle.
PF.what_to_try: Select your cycle again and restart. If it recurs with no outage, check the breaker and the circuit.
PF.when_to_call: If PF keeps appearing on a stable supply, the power board is worth checking.

codes.meaning: Sabbath Mode is active, deliberately limiting certain electronic functions for religious observance.
The unit is running in a store-display demo mode where cooling and other normal functions are disabled.
Ice has become jammed in the dispenser chute, often from partial melting and refreezing.
The refrigerator experienced a power interruption or surge.
Internal temperature has stayed too warm for over an hour, commonly from a door left ajar.
A door has remained open for more than roughly five minutes.

freezer.note: Frigidaire does not publish a separate freezer-only guide — freezers are filed under its combined refrigerator/freezer error-code guide.

codes.meaning: Fires when the freezer or fridge compartment has run too warm for more than an hour.
Power to the combined unit was lost or spiked, which can leave the freezer warmer than it should be.
One of the unit's doors has been open for an extended period.
Sabbath Mode is engaged, suppressing electronic alerts across both compartments.
On units with an ice maker in the freezer section, ice has jammed in the dispenser chute.
A key on the control's touchpad is electrically shorted, as if being held down continuously.

F1.what_it_means: A key on the control's touchpad is electrically shorted, as if it were being held down.
F1.why_it_happens: Moisture or wear in the touchpad membrane rather than anything to do with cooking.
F1.what_to_try: Cut power at the breaker for a minute. If moisture caused it, letting the panel dry can clear it.
F1.when_to_call: If it returns, the touchpad or control board needs replacing.

codes.meaning: The oven's safety logic has detected the cavity running hotter than it should, treating it as a runaway-heat condition.

F10.what_it_means: The oven's safety logic has decided the cavity is running hotter than it should and has shut the heat down as a runaway-heat condition.
F10.why_it_happens: Usually the temperature sensor misreporting, or the control calling for heat when it should not — both are component faults, not settings.
F10.what_to_try: Switch the oven off at the breaker for a minute to clear a one-off. If it returns, stop using the oven.
F10.when_to_call: Promptly, and do not keep using the oven in the meantime — the code names a heat condition the control could not govern.

codes.meaning: The oven temperature probe circuit is open, meaning the control isn't getting a signal from it.

F30.what_it_means: The oven temperature probe circuit is open — the control is getting no signal from it.
F30.why_it_happens: A broken probe or a disconnected wire, so the oven has no temperature reading to work from.
F30.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the probe circuit is internal.
F30.when_to_call: When you see it. Do not keep using an oven that cannot read its own temperature.

codes.meaning: The oven temperature probe circuit is shorted, giving the control a false reading.

F31.what_it_means: The oven temperature probe circuit is shorted, so the control is working from a false reading.
F31.why_it_happens: A shorted sensor or its wiring, rather than anything to do with how the oven is being used.
F31.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the probe circuit is internal.
F31.when_to_call: When you see it. An oven working from a false temperature reading will not cook predictably.

codes.meaning: The cooktop controls have locked themselves out and won't respond to input.
The self-clean door-locking mechanism is faulting, usually needing a power cycle to clear a false trigger.
The control boards inside the range have lost communication with one another.

F3.what_it_means: The control boards inside the range have lost communication with one another.
F3.why_it_happens: A wiring or connector fault between boards rather than a cooking fault.
F3.what_to_try: Cut power at the breaker for a minute to clear a one-off.
F3.when_to_call: If it returns after a power cycle, it needs a technician.

codes.meaning: The control cannot identify its own microprocessor, which points at the board itself.
An internal prompt/display check failed during start-up.
The cooktop controls are locked, so the surface elements will not respond until unlocked.
